title: Mirror Formula, Lens Formula and Magnification

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

expression: Mirror: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, m = −v/u  ;  Lens: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, m = v/u  ;  P = 1/f
explanation: Both mirror and lens formulas relate object distance u, image distance v, and focal length f, using the Cartesian sign convention (distances measured from the pole/optical centre, direction of incident light taken positive). Magnification m gives image size relative to object size, with its sign indicating orientation (negative = inverted). Lens power P = 1/f (in metres) is measured in dioptres, and for lenses in contact, powers simply ADD — a far more convenient way to combine multiple lenses than combining focal lengths directly.

workedExample.scenario: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm.
workedExample.result: v = 15 cm ; m = v/u = 15/(−30) = −0.5 (real, inverted, diminished image)

commonMistakes: Ignoring the sign convention and plugging in raw magnitudes — nearly all ray-optics numerical errors trace back to a wrongly signed u, v, or f.
Using the mirror magnification formula (m = −v/u) for a lens problem, or vice versa — the two formulas differ by a sign because of how each device's sign convention is set up.
genZNote: Ray optics numericals live and die by sign convention — get that wrong and everything else falls apart.
